min_supported_doc: The OLDEST Passwall-Node version this panel still tests. Everything from this row onward in released_nodes is the supported set, and that set is exactly what the released-range CI matrix exercises. MATCHED BY POSITION IN released_nodes, NOT by semver comparison: v0.0.1-beta9 sorts ABOVE v0.0.1-beta11 lexically, so comparing the strings would silently invert the floor. THIS SELECTS WHAT IS TESTED, NOT WHAT MAY CONNECT. No production code reads this field -- only the two workflows and the matrix test do -- so raising it stops testing the versions below it and does nothing else: an older node keeps syncing, and nothing refuses it for sitting below this row. Refusing a node is a separate decision about the wire generation (see wire.min_protocol_version) and needs its own change, announcement and migration acceptance; a floor move must not do that work by implication. Raising it is still BREAKING in the sense that matters here: every version below it stops being tested, so a regression in one of them stops being caught. Record it in docs/compat-policy.md's history, naming what is now untested. The field exists so the matrix can stop growing -- without a floor every release adds a permanent row.
